time series.simple: A list of numbers measured at different times, kept in time order.
time series.example: The temperature at your home, once every hour.

spaced repetition.simple: Reviewing a fact again after longer and longer breaks, so you remember it for a long time.
spaced repetition.example: A flashcard that comes back after 1, 2, 4, 8 and 16 days.

list.simple: A Python container that keeps values in order.

index.simple: The position of a value in a list (starting at 0). In pandas, the labels of the rows.

dict.simple: A Python container of key and value pairs. You look up a value by its key.

loop.simple: Code that repeats the same work for each value.
loop.example: for v in values: total = total + v

function.simple: A named block of code. It takes inputs and returns a result.

list comprehension.simple: A one-line way to build a new list from another list.
list comprehension.example: [s for s in steps if s >= 5000]

numpy.simple: The Python library for fast math on arrays of numbers.

vectorization.simple: Doing an operation on a whole array at once, without a Python loop.
vectorization.example: a * 2 doubles every value in a.

array.simple: A numpy container of same-type numbers with a fixed shape.

boolean mask.simple: An array of True and False values used to select data.
boolean mask.example: a[a > 5] keeps only the values above 5.

broadcasting.simple: The numpy rule that stretches a small array to match a bigger one in an operation.
broadcasting.example: A table of shape (3, 2) minus a vector of shape (2,) works.

nan.simple: 'Not a number': the value we use for a missing number.
nan.example: np.nan. Any sum with nan gives nan.

z-score.simple: How many standard deviations a value is above or below the mean.

standard deviation.simple: A number that tells how far values are from their mean, on average.
standard deviation.example: The values 10, 10, 10 have std 0. The values 0, 10, 20 have a bigger std.

pandas.simple: The Python library for tables of data with labels, and for time series.

Series.simple: A pandas column: values with an index of labels.

DataFrame.simple: A pandas table. Rows have an index, columns have names, and each column is a Series.

index alignment.simple: pandas matches values by index label, not by position, when you combine data. Labels with no partner give NaN.
index alignment.example: Adding a Series for days 1-3 to one for days 2-4 gives NaN on days 1 and 4.

Timestamp.simple: A value that says when an event happened. In pandas it is a Timestamp object.

Timedelta.simple: A length of time, such as 2 days or 36 hours.

DatetimeIndex.simple: A pandas index made of Timestamps. It is the standard index of a time series.

UTC.simple: The world reference time. It has no daylight saving changes.

DST.simple: Daylight saving time: clocks jump forward one hour in spring and back one hour in autumn.
DST.example: In New York a day has 23 hours in March and 25 hours in November.

rolling window.simple: A window of the last k rows that moves forward one row at a time. You compute one number per window.

moving average.simple: The mean of the last k values, computed again at each step. It smooths a series.
moving average.example: The 7-day moving average of daily sales.

data leakage.simple: Using information in a feature or in training that you would not have at prediction time. Scores look good but fail in real use.
data leakage.example: A rolling mean that includes today's value, when you predict today.
